We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: step1: sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So forward: sulfonyl chloride + amine -> sulfonamide. In retrosynthesis, we break sulfonamide to sulfonyl chloride and amine.

Our target has sulfonamide linking a tolyl sulfonyl group (p-tolyl sulfonyl?) Actually NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2 attached to a tolyl ring (first phenyl with methyl). So sulfonamide: the nitrogen attached to sulfonyl group and also attached to the tolyl ring (aniline). So disconnection: break N-S bond to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and aniline (the tolyl amine). So first retrosynthetic step: target -> sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) + aniline (p-toluidine). The sulfonyl chloride is derived from the second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) with sulfonyl chloride at para? Actually the sulfonyl group attached to that phenyl ring. So sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-Ph- (the phenyl bearing the side chain). So we need that phenyl with side chain (the unsaturated amide). So step1: break sulfonamide.

Step2: The side chain is /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide) with an extra amine on the aniline). This could be formed via Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid. Then amide formation with aniline (c3ccccc3N). So retrosynthesis: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then break the double bond formation: the α,β-unsaturated acid could be derived from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl ring c2ccc... ) and malonic acid. The aldehyde would be the phenyl ring with a formyl group at the position where the side chain attaches (i.e., 4-formyl phenyl). So step2: break amide to give unsaturated acid and aniline.

Step3: The unsaturated acid from Doebner: break to aldehyde + malonic acid. So final precursors: p-toluidine, sulfonyl chloride (from phenyl with aldehyde?), malonic acid, aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually we also need the phenyl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-CO? Wait sulfonyl chloride derived from phenyl with side chain? The sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl that also bears the side chain. So that phenyl must be functionalized with sulfonyl chloride and the side chain (the unsaturated amide). In retrosynthesis, after step2 we have the phenyl with side chain (unsaturated acid) attached to sulfonyl chloride? Actually after step2 we have the phenyl with side chain as part of the sulfonyl chloride? The sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring, and the side chain is attached to same phenyl ring at para position? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl group attached to phenyl (c2ccc...), and the side chain attached to same phenyl at para? The phenyl has two substituents: sulfonyl attached to N (coming from tolyl amine) and the side chain (α,β-unsaturated amide) attached at para position. So after breaking amide, we have phenyl with side chain as α,β-unsaturated acid attached, and also sulfonyl chloride attached (since we haven't broken sulfonamide yet). Actually step order: we can first break amide, then later break sulfonamide. But we need total 3 steps. So propose:

Step1 (retro): break amide C-N bond: target -> phenyl-sulfonyl chloride with α,β-unsaturated acid (i.e., Ar-SO2Cl with side chain as unsaturated acid) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). This is amide formation step.

Step2 (retro): break sulfonamide N-S bond: phenyl-sulfonyl chloride with side chain -> phenyl-sulfonyl chloride (same) + p-toluidine (the tolyl amine). Actually the sulfonyl chloride already present, we just separate the amine.

Step3 (retro): break the α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid (Doebner). So aldehyde is the phenyl ring with aldehyde at position where side chain attaches (i.e., 4-formyl phenyl). The sulfonyl chloride remains attached to that phenyl ring (so we need aldehyde with sulfonyl chloride substituent). So precursor: 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride (i.e., ClSO2-Ph-CHO). That's a known compound.

Thus final precursors: p-toluidine, 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride, malonic acid, aniline (c3ccccc3N). That's 4 molecules, but we have 3 reactions: (1) amide formation, (2) sulfonamide formation, (3) Doebner modification.
